speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please tell me how old you are and when you first noticed these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the exposure history and the description of painless, nonpruritic papules, I suspect molluscum contagiosum. Can you tell me if the lesions have a central dimple or umbilication, and are they flesh-colored or pearly?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation is classic for molluscum contagiosum, especially given the daycare exposure and characteristic umbilicated papules. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
